hindi: शुक्र यानी वीर्य को वहन करने वालों के दोनों स्तन, दोनों मुष्क यानी अण्डकोश और मज्जा।
english: Of those that carry śukra (semen): the two breasts, the two testicles (muṣka) and the marrow (majjā).

text_flags.why: possible: the compound is śukra-vāhin (carrier of semen); the r is missing in print

notes: Printed 'śukavāhināṃ' for śukravāhinām (r dropped), possible print slip. Elliptical: 'of the srotas' / 'the root is' is carried from units 77-82 and not supplied; the genitive is read as 'of the carriers of semen'. Whether 'carriers' are the channels (srotas) is understood from the context. The breasts are listed among semen carriers as printed; not corrected.

hindi: मूत्र को वहन करने वालों की बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय और दोनों वंक्षण यानी जाँघ के जोड़।
english: Of those that carry urine: the bladder (basti) and the two groins (vaṅkṣaṇa).
notes: Printed 'mūtravāhināṃbastir' joins two words; split without a flag as a spacing slip. basti = bladder here (the urinary bag), not the enema device. Elliptical: the 'root' is carried from units 77-82 and not supplied.

words.gloss: digested (pakva); seat (āśaya); pakvāśaya = the lower seat of digested food, large-bowel region (probable)

hindi: मल को वहन करने वालों का पक्वाशय यानी पचे हुए का स्थान, सम्भवतः बड़ी आँत का क्षेत्र और स्थूलान्त्र यानी सम्भवतः बड़ी आँत।
english: Of those that carry dung (śakṛt): the pakvāśaya (seat of the digested, probably the large-bowel region) and the thick intestine (sthūlāntra, probably the large intestine).
notes: pakvāśaya and sthūlāntra identified with the large-bowel region and large intestine: probable. Elliptical: the 'root' is carried from units 77-82 and not supplied.

hindi: स्वेद यानी पसीने को वहन करने वालों का मेद यानी चर्बी और रोमकूप यानी रोम के छिद्र।
english: Of those that carry sweat (sveda): the fat (medas) and the hair-pores (romakūpa).
notes: Printed 'svedavāhināṃmedo' joins two words (sandhi -ṃ + m); split without a flag. Elliptical: the 'root' is carried from units 77-82 and not supplied.

words.gram: tat-puruṣa (with dvandva vṛddhi-kṣaya), n. inst. sg.

hindi: इनके अनेक तरह के दूषण, अहितकर आहार और विहार यानी आचरण, उपद्रव और साधन को दोष आदि से जानना चाहिए; अपने-अपने अनुसार वृद्धि और क्षय के लक्षण से पहचानना चाहिए।
english: Of these, the various vitiation, the unwholesome food and conduct (vihāra), the complications (upadrava) and the treatment one should know through the doṣa and the rest; one should discern each by the sign of increase and decrease.
notes: The syntax is loose: 'doṣādivijñānīyāt' is read as doṣa-ādi + vijñānīyāt ('one should know ... by/as doṣa and the rest'); the instrument of knowing is not stated, so the translation keeps 'through' only as the plainest reading. Alternative: 'one should know the doṣa and the rest' as objects. 'yathāsvam' is placed with the final verb. Printed 'vijñānīyādyathāsvaṃ' joins the verb and the adverb (sandhi t + y -> d y). Alternative: 'vividham' (n. acc. sg.) may agree with 'ahitāhāravihāram' ('various unwholesome food and conduct') instead of qualifying 'dūṣaṇam'.
lines_deva: तेषां दूषणं विविधमहिताहारविहारमुपद्रवान् साधनं च दोषादिविज्ञानीयाद्यथास्वं वृद्धिक्षयलक्षणेन लक्षयेत्
lines_iast: teṣāṃ dūṣaṇaṃ vividhamahitāhāravihāramupadravān sādhanaṃ ca doṣādivijñānīyādyathāsvaṃ vṛddhikṣayalakṣaṇena lakṣayet

words.gloss: unclear (probably rudhira-śruti, flow of blood, with a stray 'ani')

hindi: स्रोतस् के वेध पर तो भ्रम, मोह, कम्प, प्रलाप, आध्मान, शूल, अरुचि, प्यास, वमन, ज्वर, अनुमानित पाठ पर रक्त का बहना, मूत्र और मल का रुकना, और मृत्यु।
english: But on the piercing of the srotas (channels): giddiness, fainting or confusion, tremor, raving, distension of the belly (ādhmāna), pain, distaste for food, thirst, vomiting, fever, on a conjectural reading flow of blood, retention of urine and stool, and death.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ani' after jvara has no clear sense; rudhira-śruti (blood flow) fits the list

notes: Damaged print: 'jvarānirudhiraśruti' is read on a conjecture as jvara + (a stray 'ani') + rudhira-śruti (flow of blood); the stray syllables are left unexplained and the 'ani' is kept unsplit as unclear. The list is read as nominatives plural/singular without a verb ('result' is understood). 'moha' = fainting or confusion. 'srotas' is a doctrinal term (body channel), kept.

hindi: इसलिए स्रोतस् में विद्ध को अस्वीकार करके उपचार करना चाहिए।
english: Therefore, having refused one pierced in a srotas, one should treat (him).

text_flags.why: possible: srotas + viddha gives srotoviddha; 'au' is a print slip

notes: Printed 'srotauviddhaṃ' is read as srotoviddham (srotas-viddha); the 'au' looks like a print slip. 'pratyākhyāya' = having declined (the case as hopeless); that one then treats is as stated. The object 'him' is understood. Alternative emendation: 'srotasi viddham' (pierced in the srotas); sense the same.

hindi: और जिसका शल्य निकाला जा चुका हो उसका सद्योव्रण की विधि से।
english: And (one) whose dart has been extracted, by the procedure for a fresh wound.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'one should treat' is carried from unit 89 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. GROUPING: appears to continue 89.

hindi: उनमें सिराएँ यानी सम्भवतः शिराएँ यानी नसें और धमनियाँ यानी स्पन्दन करने वाली वाहिकाएँ, सम्भवतः आधुनिक अर्थ की धमनियाँ, स्रोतसों के ही विशेष रूप हैं।
english: Among these, the sirā (vessels, probably veins) and the dhamanī (pulsating vessels, probably arteries) are particular forms of the srotas only.
notes: sirā and dhamanī: modern equivalents (vein, artery) are probable, not exact. The copula is understood. Printed 'sirā' is sirāḥ (visarga lost before dh, regular sandhi), plural like dhamanyaḥ.

hindi: परन्तु दूसरे अन्यता यानी भिन्नता मानते हैं।
english: But others maintain a difference (anyatva).
notes: 'anyatvam' = otherness; 'icchanti' = they wish/maintain. The 'they' (sirā, dhamanī, srotas) is understood. The printed 'anyetvanyatvam' = anye tu anyatvam.

hindi: सिरा, धमनी और स्रोतसों में केवल परस्पर निकटता, समान कर्म और सूक्ष्मता के कारण, भिन्न कर्म वाले होते हुए भी, मानो भेद का अभाव दिखाई देता है।
english: Merely through mutual proximity, similarity of function and fineness, a non-distinction, as it were, is perceived among the sirā, dhamanī and srotas, even though their functions are distinct.
notes: Printed 'avibhāgaiva' is read as avibhāga + iva (spacing slip; the Devanagari prints अविभाग इव with the vowels unjoined, the IAST 'ai' is a transliteration artefact). 'kevalam' taken with the reasons. Only a view being reported (see 92, 94).

hindi: दूसरे फिर कहते हैं।
english: Others, again, say:
notes: Opens the next view; the quotation follows in unit 95. GROUPING: appears to introduce 95.

words.gloss: rasa (the first dhātu; plasma-like fluid); carrying

hindi: स्रोतस्, सिराएँ, धमनियाँ, रसवाहिनियाँ, नाड़ियाँ, पन्थ, अयन, मार्ग, शरीर के छिद्र, बन्द और खुले, स्थान, आशय यानी आधार, क्षय यानी निवास और निकेत यानी आवास: ये शरीर में धातुओं के दिखाई देने वाले और न दिखाई देने वाले अवकाशों के नाम हैं।
english: Srotas (channels), sirā, dhamanī, the carriers of rasa, nāḍī, paths, routes, ways, openings of the body, closed and open, places, seats (āśaya), abodes and dwellings: these are the names, in the body, of the spaces of the dhātus, perceptible and imperceptible.
notes: The words after 'rasavāhinyaḥ' are all nominative plural names in a list; 'saṃvṛtāsaṃvṛtāni' (closed and open) is read with 'śarīracchidrāṇi' (openings of the body); it could also be a separate name in the list. 'rasavāhinyaḥ' = the carriers of rasa (feminine plural: vessels). Printed 'kṣayā' = kṣayāḥ; 'paṃthāno'yanāni' = panthānaḥ ayanāni. The closing 'iti' is left to notes.
lines_deva: स्रोतांसि सिरा धमन्यो रसवाहिन्यो नाड्यः पंथानोऽयनानि मार्गाः शरीरच्छिद्राणि संवृतासंवृतानि स्थानान्याशयाः क्षया निकेताश्चेति शरीरे धात्ववकाशानां लक्ष्यालक्ष्याणां नामानीति
lines_iast: srotāṃsi sirā dhamanyo rasavāhinyo nāḍyaḥ paṃthāno'yanāni mārgāḥ śarīracchidrāṇi saṃvṛtāsaṃvṛtāni sthānānyāśayāḥ kṣayā niketāśceti śarīre dhātvavakāśānāṃ lakṣyālakṣyāṇāṃ nāmānīti

hindi: और वे अवकाश।
english: And these spaces.
notes: Subject of 97; the verb is in the next unit. GROUPING: appears to continue into 97.

hindi: प्रकुपित होकर वे अपने स्थान में स्थित और मार्ग में स्थित धातुओं को प्रकुपित करते हैं।
english: Agitated, they agitate the dhātus that stand in their seats and those that stand on their paths.

text_flags.why: possible: the repeated 'sthāna' may be a print slip

notes: Printed 'sthānasthānamārgasthāṃś' is read as sthāna-sthān + mārga-sthān ('sthāna' possibly repeated by a print slip). Alternative: sthāna-sthān + a-mārga-sthān ('in place and not on their path'), which also reproduces the print exactly; the first reading is kept as the plainer one.

hindi: वे भी उन्हें और स्रोतसों को।
english: They too (agitate) those and the srotas.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'agitate' is carried from unit 97 and is not supplied. 'tān' = those dhātus (understood).

hindi: स्रोतस् और धातु धातुओं को।
english: The srotas and the dhātus (agitate) the dhātus.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'agitate' is carried from unit 97 and is not supplied.

hindi: इन सबके ही दूषित करने वाले दूषित दोष हैं।
english: The vitiators of all these indeed are the vitiated doṣas.

text_flags.why: possible: -m + eva does not give 'aiva'; the 'ai' is a print slip

notes: Printed 'sarveṣāmaiva' is read as sarveṣām eva ('ai' for 'e' looks like a print slip). 'duṣṭā' = duṣṭāḥ (visarga dropped before d in print is regular). Alternative for the printed Devanagari 'सर्वेषामैव' (real ऐ): sarveṣāṃ caiva (ca lost); 'eva' kept as the simpler guess.

hindi: और वे अधिकतर अग्नि यानी पाचन की अग्नि के दोष से दूषित होते हैं।
english: And they mostly become vitiated through a fault of agni (the digestive fire).
notes: agni = digestive fire (doctrinal term, kept). The ablative 'agnidoṣāt' = from/through a fault of agni.

words.gloss: lifespan; health; strength; growth; complexion; ojas

hindi: इसलिए निमित्त: आयु, आरोग्य, बल, उपचय यानी वृद्धि, वर्ण यानी रंगत और ओजस् यानी जीवन-सार।
english: Therefore the causes (nimitta): lifespan, health, strength, growth, complexion and ojas (vital essence).
notes: The relation is not stated: nimittāni is neuter plural and the six items are also neuter plural; it is probably 'agni is the cause of lifespan ... and ojas', but no verb or genitive is given and none is supplied. ojas = vigour (doctrinal term, kept). Read as an incomplete statement.

words.gloss: bound to that; dependent on that
rañjaka (a kind of Pitta that colours); and the rest

hindi: और उसी पर आश्रित रञ्जक यानी पित्त का एक भेद आदि, भूताग्नियाँ यानी भूतों की अग्नियाँ और धात्वग्नियाँ यानी धातुओं की अग्नियाँ हैं।
english: And dependent on that alone are the rañjaka (a kind of Pitta) and the rest, the bhūtāgnis (fires of the elements) and the dhātvagnis (fires of the dhātus).
notes: 'tat' = that agni (understood). rañjaka is the colouring kind of Pitta (standard in later Āyurveda); 'and the rest' is not listed here. Neuter 'rañjakādīni' beside masculine agnis: the list is loose. Copula understood.

hindi: वैसे ही अन्न भी उसी से पचा हुआ अमृत भाव को प्राप्त होता है और बिना पचा विष भाव को।
english: Likewise food too, digested (pakva) by that very (agni), attains the state of nectar (amṛta), and undigested, the state of poison (viṣa).
notes: Printed 'pakka' = pakva (kk spelling; orthographic normalisation). 'tena' = by that agni (understood). The verb 'attains' serves both halves.

hindi: उनमें पित्त का विशेष रूप, जिसका नाम पाचक यानी पचाने वाला है, अग्नि है, ऐसा पहले कहा गया।
english: Among these, a special kind of Pitta, named pācaka (the digesting one), is agni: so it was stated earlier.
notes: 'iti' closes the quoted statement and is rendered 'so'. The earlier statement is in an earlier part of the work and is not checked here.

hindi: दूसरे फिर कहते हैं।
english: Others, again, say:
notes: Opens the next view; the statement follows in unit 107. GROUPING: appears to introduce 107.

words.gloss: doṣa; dhātu; mala (waste); coming together; produced by

hindi: दोष, धातु और मल यानी अपशिष्ट के संयोग से उत्पन्न भीतरी ऊष्मा, जिसका स्थान और कर्म पहले बताए अनुसार हैं, अग्नि है।
english: Agni is the inner heat produced by the coming together of doṣa, dhātu and mala, whose seat and function are as indicated.
notes: Closing 'iti' marks the end of the view reported. mala = waste product (doctrinal term). 'yathānirdiṣṭa' refers to earlier statements, not checked here.

words.gloss: āmāśaya (seat of the undigested; stomach, probable); staying in

hindi: वह अग्नि, यानी भीतरी अग्नि, विधि से खाए हुए अन्न को, जिसे प्राण वायु ने कोष्ठ यानी भण्डार या पेट में खींचा है, जिसका संघात द्रवों से टूट गया है, जिसे स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा से नरम किया गया है, समान वायु से प्रज्वलित होकर, आमाशय यानी कच्चे अन्न का स्थान, सम्भवतः जठर में स्थित को, हाँडी में स्थित पानी और चावल के समान, पकाता है।
english: That agni, the inner fire, kindled by samāna (wind), cooks the food eaten according to rule, drawn into the koṣṭha (storehouse, belly) by prāṇa wind, its mass broken apart by liquids, softened by sneha (oil or fat), lying in the āmāśaya (seat of the undigested, probably the stomach) like water and rice in a pot.
notes: The sentence is long; 'abhisandhukṣitaḥ' (kindled) qualifies agni. 'sthālīsthamivāṃbutaṇḍulam' = water and rice lying in a pot (dvandva). 'agniraṃtaragniḥ' read as agniḥ + antar-agniḥ (agni, the inner fire). The wind names prāṇa and samāna are doctrinal. āmāśaya = stomach: probable.
lines_deva: स खलु विधिवदभ्यवहृतमन्नजातंप्राणेन वायुना कोष्ठमाकृष्टं द्रवैर्विभिन्नसंघातं स्नेहेन मृदूकृतमभिसंधुक्षितः समानेनामाशयस्थं स्थालीस्थमिवांबुतंडुलमग्निरंतरग्निःपचति
lines_iast: sa khalu vidhivadabhyavahṛtamannajātaṃprāṇena vāyunā koṣṭhamākṛṣṭaṃ dravairvibhinnasaṃghātaṃ snehena mṛdūkṛtamabhisaṃdhukṣitaḥ samānenāmāśayasthaṃ sthālīsthamivāṃbutaṃḍulamagniraṃtaragniḥpacati

words.gram: pres. pass. part. √pac, n. nom. sg.
loc. sg. of ādi, as ind.

hindi: वह अन्न तो, सब रसों यानी स्वादों वाला होते हुए भी, पकते समय पहले मधुर हो जाकर फेनिल हुए कफ को उभारता है।
english: That (food), however, though containing all tastes (rasa), as it is being cooked, first becomes sweet and stirs up Kapha, become foamy.

text_flags.why: possible: 'tas' has no sense here; neuter 'tat' (the food) agrees with pacyamānam

notes: Printed 'tastu' is read as tat tu (the food is the subject; the participles are neuter singular). 'sarvarasa' = having all tastes. udīrayati = stirs up (sets in motion).
lines_deva: तस्तु सर्वरसमपि पच्यमानमादौ मधुरीभूतं कफं फेनीभूतमूदीरयति
lines_iast: tastu sarvarasamapi pacyamānamādau madhurībhūtaṃ kaphaṃ phenībhūtamūdīrayati

hindi: तब जला हुआ, खट्टा हो गया, आमाशय से खिसकता हुआ, स्वच्छ पित्त को।
english: Then, burnt (vidagdha), turned sour, falling away from the āmāśaya, (it stirs up) clear Pitta.
notes: Elliptical: the verb udīrayati (stirs up) is carried from unit 109 and is not supplied. The subject (the food) is understood; vidagdha = burnt/overcooked, rendered literally. accha = clear.

words.gloss: digested; seat; pakvāśaya (lower seat of the digested, large-bowel region; probable)

hindi: और पक्वाशय यानी सम्भवतः बड़ी आँत के क्षेत्र में पहुँचकर तीखा हो गया, अनिल यानी वात को।
english: And having reached the pakvāśaya (probably the large-bowel region), turned pungent, (it stirs up) the wind (anila, that is Vāta).
notes: Elliptical: the verb udīrayati (stirs up) is carried from unit 109 and is not supplied. 'anila' = wind, here the humour Vāta in context.

hindi: और तब इस प्रकार आहार के भीगकर नरम हो जाने पर, पाँच, अस्पष्ट शब्द, वायु से अलग-अलग किए हुए, अनुमानित पाठ पर, अपने-अपने अनुसार आहार में स्थित पाँच ही भूत-गुणों को पकाते हैं।
english: And then, the food being thus moistened, five (unclear words), scattered by wind, each according to its own, cook, on a conjectural reading, only the five element-qualities (bhūtaguṇa) lying in the food.

text_flags.why: possible: the locative absolute is 'viklinne āhāre'; the print leaves the vowels unjoined
possible: damaged print; restoration only a guess, not adopted in the translation

notes: Damaged print: 'paṃcātamaka mahābhūtana mayo' are kept unsplit as unclear; a possible restoration is 'pañcātmakāḥ mahābhūtāgnayaḥ' (the five fires of the great elements, which would give the plural subject of 'pacanti'), but this is not adopted. The grammar of 'vyastāni' and the subject of 'pacanti' are therefore uncertain. Printed 'viklinnaāhāre' is read as viklinne āhāre (the vowels are not joined in print). Compare the bhūtāgnis in unit 103. The neuter plural 'vyastāni' suggests a neuter subject (such as mahābhūtāni) rather than the masculine 'mahābhūtāgnayaḥ'; the restoration is a guess only.
lines_deva: ततश्चैवं विक्लिन्नआहारे पंच पंचातमक महाभूतन मयो वायुना व्यस्तान्यथास्वं पंचैवभूतगुणानाहारस्थान् पचंति
lines_iast: tataścaivaṃ viklinnaāhāre paṃca paṃcātamaka mahābhūtana mayo vāyunā vyastānyathāsvaṃ paṃcaivabhūtaguṇānāhārasthān pacaṃti

hindi: वे पके हुए फिर अपने-अपने अनुसार ही शरीर में स्थित और अपने अविकृत रूप वाले भूत-गुणों को पुष्ट करते हैं।
english: Those, cooked, again, each according to its own, nourish the element-qualities (bhūtaguṇa) that rest in the body and are of their own unaltered nature.
notes: 'svāvikārabhūtān' is read as sva-avikāra-bhūtān ('being of their own unaltered nature'); the alternative sva-vikāra-bhūtān ('being their own modifications') is possible. 'te' = the five element-qualities (understood from 112).
lines_deva: ते पक्काः पुनर्यथास्वमेव देहाश्रितांश्च स्वाविकारभूतान् भूतगुणानाप्याययंति
lines_iast: te pakkāḥ punaryathāsvameva dehāśritāṃśca svāvikārabhūtān bhūtaguṇānāpyāyayaṃti

hindi: और इस प्रकार पके हुए आहार से, मानो अनेक औषधों को भीतर रखने वाले स्नेह से, रस नामक स्वच्छ सार और किट्ट नामक मल उत्पन्न होता है।
english: And thus, from the digested food, as if from an oil having various medicines in its core, a clear essence named rasa and a waste (mala) named kiṭṭa are produced.
notes: The simile 'vividhauṣadhagarbhād iva snehāt' (as if from an oil with various medicinal substances inside) is kept literal; its exact point is not stated. 'pakka' = pakva (kk spelling). 'kiṭṭa' = refuse of food. The verb is singular for two subjects.
lines_deva: एवं च पक्कादाहाराद्विविधौषधगर्भादिव स्नेहादच्छः सारभूतो रसाख्यः किट्टाख्यश्चमलोऽभिनिर्वर्तते
lines_iast: evaṃ ca pakkādāhārādvividhauṣadhagarbhādiva snehādacchaḥ sārabhūto rasākhyaḥ kiṭṭākhyaścamalo'bhinirvartate

words.gram: bahuvrīhi, m. acc. sg. as ind.

hindi: और उन सार और मल दोनों से, उसी स्वरूप वाले, धातु नामक शारीरिक गुणों के स्रोतस् अपने-अपने अनुसार क्रम से अटूट प्रवाह में भरे जाते हैं।
english: And by those two, the essence and the waste, the srotas of the bodily qualities having just that nature, named dhātus, are each filled in succession in an unbroken stream.

text_flags.why: possible: dhātu + ākhyāna gives dhātvākhyāna; the printed 'dhātuv-' has a stray u

notes: Printed 'dhātuvākhyānāṃ' is read as dhātvākhyānām (extra 'u'). 'śārīraguṇa' (bodily qualities) is a loose term for the dhātus here. The sense of 'tadātmaka' (having the nature of those) is plain; the exact relation of 'sāra' to the dhātus is not spelt out.
lines_deva: ताभ्यां च सारमलाभ्यां तदात्मकानामेव शारीरगुणानां धातुवाख्यानां यथास्वं स्रोतांसि पारंपर्येणाव्यवच्छिन्नसंतानमापूर्यंते
lines_iast: tābhyāṃ ca sāramalābhyāṃ tadātmakānāmeva śārīraguṇānāṃ dhātuvākhyānāṃ yathāsvaṃ srotāṃsi pāraṃparyeṇāvyavacchinnasaṃtānamāpūryaṃte

hindi: और स्रोतसों से विभाग के अनुसार, आवश्यकता के अनुसार ही धातु पुष्ट होते हैं।
english: And from the srotas, according to division and according to need, the dhātus are nourished.

text_flags.why: possible: 'yathātham' is not a word; yathārtham (according to need) fits

notes: Printed 'strotobhyaḥ' for srotobhyaḥ (orthographic normalisation recorded in the glossary). 'yathāthameva' is read as yathārtham eva ('according to need'); the r is lost in print.

words.gram: pres. mid. part. ā-√pyāy, n. gen. pl.

hindi: बाद-बाद वाले के प्रवेश करने पर भी, समय पर आहार के ठीक सेवन से परिणाम के साथ पोषित होते हुए पहले वाले स्रोतसों का क्षय नहीं होता।
english: Even with the successive entry of each later one, there is no wasting (apacaya) of the earlier srotas, which are nourished in due time by the proper use of food, with transformation.
notes: Printed 'pariṇāmavatāpyāyamānānāṃ' is read as pariṇāmavat + āpyāyamānānām. 'uttarottarānupraveśa' (each later one entering the earlier) is read loosely as the later stages drawing on the earlier ones; the wording leaves the exact process unstated. Not translated further.
lines_deva: उत्तरोत्तरानुप्रवेशेऽपि च पूर्वेषां स्रोतसां यथाकालं सम्यगाहारोपयोगेन परिणामवताप्यायमानानां नापचयो भवति
lines_iast: uttarottarānupraveśe'pi ca pūrveṣāṃ srotasāṃ yathākālaṃ samyagāhāropayogena pariṇāmavatāpyāyamānānāṃ nāpacayo bhavati

words.gram: avyayībhāva/dvandva, n. acc. sg. as ind.

hindi: और तब धातु नामक प्रसाद यानी निर्मल सार और मल यानी अपशिष्ट अपने-अपने मान यानी माप का ही अनुसरण करते हैं, आयु और शरीर के अनुसार।
english: And then the clear essences (prasāda) and the wastes (mala) called dhātus each follow their own measure, according to age and body.
notes: 'dhātvākhyāḥ prasādamalāḥ' = the clear essences and wastes named dhātus (loose); 'yathāvayaḥśarīram' = according to age and body. Doctrinal terms prasāda and mala kept.

words.gram: pres. pass. part. √pac, m. nom. sg.

words.gloss: own; nature, state; loss; immediately after

hindi: वहाँ आहार-रस, व्यान यानी शरीर में फैलने वाली वायु से बिखेरा हुआ, अपने-अपने अनुसार सम होकर — पाठ अनिश्चित —, धातुओं की अग्नियों में क्रम से पकता हुआ, अपने स्वरूप के छूटने के तुरन्त बाद, प्राम्रक्तादि — यह शब्द अस्पष्ट है — धातु नाम वाला, यथासमय अटूट बल-परिमाण वाला होकर, शरीर को पुष्ट करके, धातुओं और धातुओं के मलों को पोषित करता है।
english: There, the food-rasa (āhāra-rasa), scattered by vyāna (a wind), each according to its own, even (reading uncertain), being cooked in order in the dhātu-fires, immediately after the loss of its own state, bearing the dhātu name 'prāmraktādi' (unclear), timely and of unfailing measure of strength, having invigorated the body, nourishes the dhātus and the wastes of the dhātus.

text_flags.why: possible: damaged print; conjectural, not adopted
possible: reading uncertain; samaḥ tu or samastaḥ tu

notes: Damaged print: 'prāmraktādi' is kept unsplit as unclear (a guess: rasa-rakta-ādi, 'rasa, blood and the rest', as the dhātu names), not adopted. 'samastu' is read as samaḥ tu (regular sandhi) with an uncertain sense; the alternative samastaḥ tu ('as a whole, however') would need a lost visarga. vyāna is the pervading wind (doctrinal). The parse of the long participial chain is therefore provisional.
lines_deva: तत्राहाररसो व्यानविक्षिप्तो यथास्वं समस्तु धात्वग्निषु क्रमात्पच्यमानः स्वात्मभावप्रच्युतिसमनंतरमेव प्राम्रक्तादिधातुसंज्ञकः कालवदस्खलितबलप्रमाणो देहमूर्जयित्वा धातून्धातुमलांश्च पुष्णाति
lines_iast: tatrāhāraraso vyānavikṣipto yathāsvaṃ samastu dhātvagniṣu kramātpacyamānaḥ svātmabhāvapracyutisamanaṃtarameva prāmraktādidhātusaṃjñakaḥ kālavadaskhalitabalapramāṇo dehamūrjayitvā dhātūndhātumalāṃśca puṣṇāti

hindi: अब अन्न का किट्ट यानी अपशिष्ट: स्वच्छ मूत्र और घना मल।
english: Now the refuse of food (anna-kiṭṭa): clear urine (mūtra) and thick dung (śakṛt).
notes: Copula understood. The two items are read as the two kinds of food-refuse; 'accham' and 'ghanam' qualify mūtra and śakṛt respectively.

hindi: रस का सार रक्त है; मल कफ और लसीका यानी सम्भवतः ऊतक-द्रव है।
english: Of rasa the essence is blood (rakta); the waste (mala) is Kapha and lasīkā (probably lymph or tissue fluid).
notes: Printed 'kafo' = kaphaḥ (f for ph, nukta spelling; print habit, normalised). The meaning of lasīkā as lymph is probable, not certain. Copula understood.
lines_deva: रसस्य सारो रक्तं मलः कफ़ो लसीका च
lines_iast: rasasya sāro raktaṃ malaḥ kafo lasīkā ca

hindi: रक्त का सार मांस है; कण्डराएँ यानी सम्भवतः बड़े टेंडन और सिराएँ भी; मल पित्त है।
english: Of blood the essence is flesh (māṃsa); the tendons (kaṇḍarā, probably large tendons) and the vessels (sirā) too; the waste is Pitta.
notes: Whether kaṇḍarā and sirā are part of the 'essence' or a separate product is not stated; the words are given as printed after the essence and before the waste. Copula understood.
lines_deva: रक्तस्य सारो मांसं कंडराः सिराश्च मलः पित्तं
lines_iast: raktasya sāro māṃsaṃ kaṃḍarāḥ sirāśca malaḥ pittaṃ

words.gloss: ear; eye; nose; mouth; hair; pore; genital organ

hindi: मांस का सार मेद यानी चर्बी, त्वचाएँ और वसा यानी मांस की चर्बी है; किट्ट कान, आँख, नाक, मुख, रोमकूप और जननेन्द्रिय के मल हैं।
english: Of flesh the essence is fat (medas), the skins (tvacaḥ, plural) and vasā (muscle fat); the refuse is the wastes of the ear, eye, nose, mouth, hair-pores and genital organ.
notes: The print leaves a space before 'malāḥ' (karṇākṣi...prajanana malāḥ) though it is one compound; read as one. 'tvacaḥ' taken as nominative plural (layers of skin). 'prajanana' = generative organ. Copula understood.
lines_deva: मांसस्यसारो मेदस्त्वचो वसा च किट्टं कर्णाक्षिनासिकास्यरोमकूपप्रजनन मलाः
lines_iast: māṃsasyasāro medastvaco vasā ca kiṭṭaṃ karṇākṣināsikāsyaromakūpaprajanana malāḥ
